extensions.name: Alacritty
extensions.description: Alacritty, the fast open-source terminal written in Rust (Apache-2.0 or MIT), as its own window inside a card, one per card; the terminals linked to it type command lines into it. Installing it downloads Alacritty 0.17.0 for Windows (6 MB, its portable program from Alacritty's GitHub release, checked against the pinned sha256).

extensions.name: Orkestri Files
extensions.description: A local web app in a card: Python's http.server, a stand-in for VSCodium's serve-web.

extensions.name: Jupyter
extensions.description: Jupyter notebook cells on the canvas: Python code cells linked into pipelines on a real kernel, run by you or by linked terminals (orkestri cell). Installing it downloads a portable CPython 3.12.16 (21 MB, pinned sha256) and installs ipykernel 7.4.0 into it, inside Orkestri's profile (about 170 MB): no Python needed on the computer, nothing system-wide. Not made or endorsed by Project Jupyter.

extensions.name: Lucid Volcano
extensions.author: Marcos Gabriel
extensions.description: Lava (greys) and Magma (navy) with a pink-red accent: the colours of Lucid Volcano, the VS Code theme by Marcos Gabriel (MarcosGabriel.lucid-volcano), mapped to Orkestri. The original states no licence, so this package holds none of its files: only its palette, with credit.

extensions.name: n8n
extensions.description: n8n, the workflow automation tool (fair-code, Sustainable Use License), on this computer only, its editor in a card; linked terminals list, create and run workflows and read executions. Installing it uses the computer's Node.js 24 or downloads the official portable Node.js 24.22.3 (36 MB, pinned sha256), then installs n8n 2.48.6 from npm into Orkestri's profile (about 2.6 GB, a few minutes). Not made or endorsed by n8n GmbH.

extensions.name: Orkestri Sépia
extensions.description: A warm paper theme: sepia surfaces, brown ink, a sienna accent.

extensions.name: VSCodium
extensions.description: VSCodium, the open-source build of VS Code (MIT), as its own window inside a card, one per card; linked terminals drive it (orkestri code). Installing it downloads the portable VSCodium 1.143.17232 for Windows x64 (221 MB) from its GitHub release, checked against the pinned sha256.

extensions.name: WezTerm
extensions.description: WezTerm, the open-source terminal written in Rust (MIT), as its own window inside a card, one per card; the terminals linked to it type command lines into it and read its screen. Installing it downloads WezTerm 20240203-110809-5046fc22 for Windows (66 MB, its portable zip from WezTerm's GitHub release, checked against the pinned sha256).

extensions.name: Zed
extensions.description: Zed, the open-source code editor written in Rust, as its own window inside a card, one per card. Installing it downloads the official Zed 1.29.2 for Windows x64 (62 MB, its installer from Zed's GitHub release, signed by Zed Industries and checked against the pinned sha256) and innounp, which unpacks it into Orkestri's own folder: nothing is installed on the computer.
